questions.q: What does AWR capture, and how often does it do so by default?
options: Instance-wide performance data such as wait events, SQL stats, and time model data, captured as a snapshot roughly every 60 minutes
Only the text of the ten slowest queries, captured once per day
A full backup of every table, captured every 60 minutes
Nothing automatically — every snapshot must be triggered manually
questions.explain: AWR takes scheduled snapshots (default every 60 minutes) of broad instance-wide performance data, stored in SYSAUX with an 8-day default retention.

questions.q: How does ASH (Active Session History) sample data, and why does that matter for diagnosing a short spike?
options: It samples every active session's state once per second, which can catch a brief spike that an hourly AWR summary would average away
It samples once per hour, identical to AWR, so it offers no additional detail
It only samples idle sessions, never active ones
It samples once per day at midnight
questions.explain: ASH's per-second sampling of active sessions preserves fine-grained detail that a coarser hourly AWR aggregate would smooth over.

questions.q: Where does live ASH data reside, and where does historical ASH data get persisted for longer retention?
options: Live in a circular buffer in the SGA, queryable via V$ACTIVE_SESSION_HISTORY, with a subset persisted into AWR as DBA_HIST_ACTIVE_SESS_HISTORY
Live data is written directly to a flat text log file only
Both live and historical ASH data live exclusively in the SYSTEM tablespace
ASH has no historical component at all — only live data exists
questions.explain: V$ACTIVE_SESSION_HISTORY exposes current in-memory samples; a subset is flushed into AWR's DBA_HIST_ACTIVE_SESS_HISTORY for longer-term retention.

questions.q: How do AWR and ASH differ from SQL Server's Query Store in scope and licensing?
options: AWR/ASH cover the entire time model and wait events, not just query plans, and require the licensed Diagnostics Pack option on Enterprise Edition, unlike Query Store which needs no separate license
AWR and ASH are free in every Oracle edition and cover only query plans, identical to Query Store
Query Store requires a separate paid license while AWR and ASH are always free
There is no meaningful difference between the two systems
questions.explain: AWR/ASH capture a broader system-wide picture than Query Store's per-query focus, but that breadth comes with a real licensing requirement: the Diagnostics Pack.

questions.q: A user reports the app felt slow for about 90 seconds, but the hourly AWR snapshot for that window looks unremarkable. What should you check instead, and why?
options: ASH, because its per-second sampling can reveal a short-lived spike that got averaged away in the hourly AWR summary
Nothing further is possible — if AWR shows nothing, the issue didn't happen
RMAN backup logs, since they track session-level wait events
The alert log only, since it always contains performance spike details
questions.explain: ASH's second-by-second granularity is specifically suited to catching brief spikes that an hourly AWR aggregate can mask.
